interest: Shows postwar US reparations advisers for Japan, and Ambassador Stewart's advocacy for American industrial help to stabilize Formosa.
overview: File (1946-48): Martin discusses Australian experts for Japan's reparations work; Stewart and Butterworth debate Formosa unrest after retrocession, recommending American adviser Armstrong and private capital to stabilize the island against communism.

people.name: Edwin M. Martin
people.role: Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

people.name: George H. Kerr
people.role: Former U.S. Vice Consul and diplomatic observer on Formosa

people.name: William Walton Butterworth
people.role: Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

people.name: George S. Armstrong
people.role: Industrial engineering consultant and proposed industrial adviser

people.name: Chiang Kai-shek
people.role: President / Generalissimo of the Republic of China

subfiles.about: Interim reply to Australia regarding an offer to provide economic and engineering specialists for Japanese reparations work.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Martin tells Plimsoll Australia's offer of reparations experts awaits a Patterson committee decision, with thanks.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Major J. Plimsoll on Australian Experts for Japanese Reparations
subfiles.to: Major J. Plimsoll, Australian Delegate, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Detailed assessment of unrest in Formosa and a recommendation to recruit an American industrial adviser to guide economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.from: J. Leighton Stewart, U.S. Ambassador to China
subfiles.summary: Stewart confirms Kerr's report of Formosan discontent, blaming mainland mismanagement and centralization, and recommends industrial adviser Armstrong and ventures like Reynolds Aluminum to stabilize the island against communism.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ambassador J. Leighton Stewart to W. Walton Butterworth on Conditions in Formosa and Proposed Industrial Adviser
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Instructions advising that Chinese authorities must formally initiate the request for an American industrial adviser before the U.S. assists.
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State (drafted by W. Walton Butterworth)
subfiles.summary: Marshall tells Stewart Chinese authorities, not the US, should formally request adviser Armstrong's recruitment.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Secretary of State Marshall (Butterworth) to Embassy Nanking on Industrial Adviser for Formosa
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Nanking (for Ambassador J. Leighton Stewart)
